<h1 class="csf-hero__title">Cakes you can make in a <em>bedroom</em>.</h1>

<p class="csf-hero__lede">
These are the desserts we make together, and they're all chosen for the same reasons:
<strong>they're cheap, they're easy, and a bowl, a spoon and a fridge are all you need.</strong>
Learn one with us, then make it again on your own.
</p>

::: {.csf-section}
<p class="csf-section__kicker">our favourites</p>
<h2 class="csf-section__title">Desserts, because heat is the thing we don't have</h2>
<p class="csf-section__sub">
Dessert is where cooking without fire stops being a limit and starts being an
advantage. A lot of the best ones were never baked anyway.
</p>

::: {.csf-grid}
::: {.csf-card .csf-card--cocoa}
<span class="csf-card__icon"><i class="bi bi-cookie"></i></span>

### Salame di cioccolato
The one we make most. Crush dry biscuits in a bag, melt dark chocolate with butter, mix
with a little sugar, roll it into a log in baking paper and chill it. It slices like a
salami and it never fails.

<p class="csf-card__facts"><span><i class="bi bi-basket"></i> 4 ingredients</span><span><i class="bi bi-snow"></i> 2 hours in the fridge</span></p>
:::

::: {.csf-card .csf-card--butter}
<span class="csf-card__icon"><i class="bi bi-cup-hot-fill"></i></span>

### Tiramisù
No-bake by definition. Mascarpone, eggs, sugar, coffee, savoiardi, cocoa. The only hard
part is not tipping the tray on the way to the fridge.

<p class="csf-card__facts"><span><i class="bi bi-basket"></i> 6 ingredients</span><span><i class="bi bi-snow"></i> a few hours in the fridge</span></p>
:::

::: {.csf-card .csf-card--berry}
<span class="csf-card__icon"><i class="bi bi-cake2-fill"></i></span>

### No-bake cheesecake
A crushed biscuit and butter base pressed into a tin, cream cheese whipped with sugar
and lemon on top, then hours of doing nothing at all. Looks like the hardest thing here;
it's the easiest.

<p class="csf-card__facts"><span><i class="bi bi-basket"></i> 5 ingredients</span><span><i class="bi bi-snow"></i> a few hours in the fridge</span></p>
:::

::: {.csf-card .csf-card--blue}
<span class="csf-card__icon"><i class="bi bi-cup-straw"></i></span>

### Two-ingredient chocolate mousse
Dark chocolate and cream, whipped. That's the whole recipe. The whisking gets passed
around the table, which is half the fun.

<p class="csf-card__facts"><span><i class="bi bi-basket"></i> 2 ingredients</span><span><i class="bi bi-people"></i> whisking shared out</span></p>
:::

::: {.csf-card .csf-card--pista}
<span class="csf-card__icon"><i class="bi bi-apple"></i></span>

### Fruit with lemon and sugar
Chop whatever's in season, add sugar and lemon juice, and in thirty minutes it makes its
own syrup. Costs almost nothing, and everybody takes some.

<p class="csf-card__facts"><span><i class="bi bi-basket"></i> 3 ingredients</span><span><i class="bi bi-clock"></i> 30 minutes</span></p>
:::

::: {.csf-card .csf-card--cocoa}
<span class="csf-card__icon"><i class="bi bi-snow2"></i></span>

### Affogato
Very cold vanilla ice cream, very hot espresso poured over it at the table. Less a
recipe, more a reliable way to end an evening.

<p class="csf-card__facts"><span><i class="bi bi-basket"></i> 2 ingredients</span><span><i class="bi bi-clock"></i> 1 minute</span></p>
:::
:::

Sometimes something savoury sneaks in before the sugar: a lazy hummus mashed with a
fork, a panzanella, a grated carrot and orange salad, a board of cheese and fruit. Same
rule: nothing goes near a flame.
:::

::: {.csf-split}
::: {}
<p class="csf-section__kicker">how we pick them</p>
<h2 class="csf-section__title">Why these and not others</h2>
<p class="csf-section__sub">
A recipe has to pass four tests before it makes it onto our table.
</p>

Got a favourite no-bake dessert that passes all four? Bring the idea (not the dessert)
to the next session.
:::

::: {.csf-checks}
- **Nothing needs heat.** No oven, no stove, no waiting for a shared kitchen to free up.
- **It's cheap.** Supermarket basics that feed a whole table without anyone chipping in.
- **The steps split up.** Someone crushes, someone melts, someone rolls. If only one pair
  of hands can make it, it's the wrong recipe for a group.
- **You can make it again alone.** In a bedroom with a fridge down the hall, which is the
  whole point.
:::
:::
:::
